title: Macroscopic Nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer Mediated by Coherent Magnons
abstract: Phonon-mediated nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer (RET) in metal deuterides is severely constrained by inertial rest-mass dilution, lattice fracture limits, and thermal nuclear spin cancellation. Extending the generalized nuclear Dicke model to Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) magnons eliminates mass dilution via hyperfine-amplified M1 coupling while unlocking relativistic Dirac M2 coupling via Overhauser spin polarization. We derive a Suhl-clamped FMR scaling law predicting 14.2 MeV (Pd-106) and 11.4 MeV (Ni-58) breakup neutrons, 19.9 MeV alpha particles, and reconciled sub-keV fusion anomalies.
summary: This theoretical paper models macroscopic Nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer (RET) in metal deuterides using coherent magnons instead of phonons. By incorporating FMR-driven Overhauser polarization, the model overcomes previous physical limitations, leading to a derived scaling law that predicts specific high-energy particle emissions and reconciles several observed fusion anomalies.
main_problem: The paper addresses the discrepancy between the predicted and observed rates of Nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer (RET) in metal deuterides, particularly in the context of solid-state fusion.
main_result: The authors derive a Suhl-clamped FMR scaling law, predicting specific high-energy breakup neutrons (e.g., 14.2 MeV for Pd-106) and reconciling multiple fusion anomalies.
method: The study extends the generalized nuclear Dicke model by replacing phonon mediation with coherent magnon mediation driven by Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR).
model_or_system: The system involves a Donor ($	ext{D}_2 	o {}^4	ext{He}$), a Coherent Magnon Bath ($\hbar\omega_M$), and a Heavy Acceptor ($	ext{Pd}/	ext{Ni}$), modeled using a Hamiltonian incorporating hyperfine-amplified M1 and M2 couplings.
key_observables: Predicted breakup neutron energies (14.2 MeV, 11.4 MeV), alpha particle energy (19.9 MeV), and the transfer rate scaling $\Gamma_{	ext{transfer}}(f_M) \propto f_M^{-10.82}$.
important_parameters: Suhl limit ($h_{	ext{crit}}$), critical frequency ($f_{	ext{crit}}$), and the effective magnetic energy density ($u_{	ext{Suhl}}$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that coherent magnon excitation via FMR and Overhauser DNP overcomes limitations imposed by phonon mediation, such as mass dilution and thermal spin cancellation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the three-zone quantum pathway for Magnon-RET, detailing the coupling between the donor, magnon bath, and heavy acceptor.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the limitations of phonon-mediated RET, then introducing the magnon-mediated model via FMR, deriving the necessary scaling laws, and finally applying this framework to reconcile multiple experimental anomalies.
why_interesting: The work provides a highly detailed, quantum-mechanical framework for energy transfer in condensed matter systems, linking magnetic excitations (magnons) to nuclear reaction rates, which has parallels in open quantum systems dynamics.
